tasks.desc: Prove the even-block lemma: for 2m elements, max score = sum largest m - sum smallest m, using a sign upper bound and an adjacent opposite-color pairing construction.

Prove the odd-N structure: the final remaining element must have odd 1-based index, no pair can cross it, and for a fixed odd separator the optimum is the sum of the even-block optima of the left and right parts.

Implement a complete runnable Python 3 program that reads stdin and prints the answer, using the proven formula and a two-heap half-maintainer for even-block scores, with O(N log N) time and fast I/O.
Validate the implementation on the provided samples; the sample tests passed and the heap invariant/indexing matches the proven formula.

proposals: Pursue the non-crossing-matching-to-half-sum reduction and compute prefix and suffix half-sums with two heaps as the primary implementation.
Implement a Fenwick-tree order-statistic version with coordinate compression and kth-rank search as an alternative or cross-check for the same prefix and suffix values.
Consider an offline wavelet tree or persistent segment tree for range top-k sum queries if a more general query structure is desired and memory allows.
Build a small-N interval DP or brute-force matcher to validate the even-block half-sum formula and the odd-index separator rule on random tests.

Keep the sign-assignment, convex L1, threshold-integral, and greedy ideas as conceptual checks or sanity tests only, since they have serious pitfalls and are less likely to yield the clean scalable solution.
prev: Implement a complete runnable Python 3 program that reads stdin and prints the answer, using the proven formula: even N = sum largest N/2 - sum smallest N/2; odd N = max over even prefix length l of even-block score of a[0:l] plus even-block score of a[l+1:n], using a two-heap half-maintainer and suffix scores; then run it on the three samples to confirm outputs 5, 14, 0.
